date.locator: Vol. VIII, no. 6, September 1850, p. 312, opening paragraph and closing dateline
date.note: Opening paragraph states Friday, July 26. The closing dateline reads July 19; retain the conflict rather than treating this as a settled exact date.

date.locator: Vol. VIII, no. 4, July 1850, p. 202, opening paragraph
date.note: The annual meeting is explicitly dated Sunday, May 12, 1850. The issue month is July, not the event date.
The editorial describes the Rosh Hashanah dispute after Wise’s dismissal on September 5. This supports September 1850, without specifying a day for the confrontation.

documented.locator: Vol. I, no. 2 (May 1843), opening paragraphs and curriculum list
documented.note: 1843 is the report year, not the founding year. The writer also recalls visiting in the preceding November.

founded.note: 1842 is derived from the report’s relative dating, “about this time last year”; no exact founding day is claimed.

founded.locator: Vol. I, no. 8 (November 1843), section “The United Hebrew Beneficent Society”
founded.note: The foundation year is explicit in the notice; it is not the 1843 election year.

founded.locator: Vol. I, no. 8 (November 1843), section “The United Hebrew Beneficent Fuel and Savings Society”
founded.note: The source explicitly gives February 1841. Its March 1843 officer election is a separate date.

documented.locator: Vol. I, no. 9 (December 1843), title and opening report, including the paragraph beginning “Our Report states forty-four children”
documented.note: 1843 dates the published annual report. No founding year is assigned from anniversary arithmetic.

founded.note: The foundation year 1839 is explicitly stated. The issue date and the anniversary dinner are not founding dates.

documented.locator: Vol. I, no. 10 (January 1844), title and opening paragraph
documented.note: The December 14 anniversary described in the January 1844 issue documents activity in 1843. A founding year is left unset.

founded.locator: Vol. I, no. 10 (January 1844), “New Societies in Philadelphia”, first paragraph
founded.note: The October 11 date is read as the preceding October, 1843, in this January 1844 report; the day is not stored as a separate exact founding date.

documented.locator: Vol. I, no. 10 (January 1844), “New Societies in Philadelphia”, second society notice
documented.note: 1844 is the publication year documenting the organization. It is distinct from the Mercy and Truth society in the preceding paragraph.

documented.locator: Vol. I, no. 10 (January 1844), “Officers”, entry “Ladies’ Benevolent Society”
documented.note: The notice documents the society in January 1844. It gives officers, not a founding date.

documented.locator: Vol. I, no. 10 (January 1844), “Officers”, entry “Society for Indigent Old Men”
documented.note: 1844 is the date of the published officer list. No institutional lifespan or separate building is inferred.

documented.locator: Vol. I, no. 10 (January 1844), “Officers”, entry headed גמילות חסד
documented.note: The published list documents the society in 1844. Its shared Hebrew terminology does not identify it with a Philadelphia organization.

documented.locator: Vol. I, no. 11 (February 1844), “Elections”, first annual-meeting notice; Volume I contents index entry identifies Philadelphia
documented.note: The meeting date is December 24, 1843; February 1844 is the publication date. Locality is supplied by the archive’s contents-index label.

documented.locator: Vol. I, no. 11 (February 1844), “Elections”, notice beginning “At the annual meeting of the Hebrew Benevolent Society of Cincinnati”
documented.note: 1844 is the report year. The original foundation date Heshvan 5603 is retained in the description rather than silently converted.

founded.locator: Vol. I, no. 9 (December 1843), “Female Hebrew Benevolent Society”, opening report recalling autumn 1819
founded.note: The society’s report describes its organizing initiative in autumn 1819. This adds a contemporary institutional account to the existing secondary reference.
